title: Undated respiratory theory photographs posted 2025-09-05
note: Seven preferred photographs, 42 questions: physiology 1-22, anatomy 1-12, histology 1-5 and embryology 1-3. Source stars identify selections but are not an official key. Wording overlaps the separate 42-item photo paper; each supplied version is retained with its own numbering and marks.

questions.prompt: Contraction of which one of the following muscles depresses the chest cage?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Abdominal recti depress the ribs during active expiration.

questions.prompt: What is the normal pleural pressure at the beginning and end of normal inspiration, respectively?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Pleural pressure becomes more negative during inspiration: approximately -5 to -7.5 cmH2O.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following agents leads to a decrease in resistance of airways?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Epinephrine relaxes bronchiolar smooth muscle through beta-2 receptors.

questions.prompt: What is the most important factor affecting lung compliance?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the course comparison, air-liquid surface tension contributes the larger share of lung recoil. Airway resistance is distinct from static compliance.

questions.prompt: What is the "Functional Residual Capacity"?
options: The volume of air remaining in the lungs after the most forceful expiration
The maximum amount of air a person can expel from the lungs after first filling the lungs to their maximum extent
The amount of air that remains in the lungs at the end of normal expiration
The maximum extra volume of air that can be expired by forceful expiration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: FRC is the volume remaining after normal passive expiration (ERV + RV).

questions.prompt: Which zone of the lung has no blood flow during both of systole and diastole phases?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Zone 1 has alveolar pressure above vascular pressures and no flow. It is not an obligatory zone in a healthy upright lung.

questions.prompt: What is the mean pulmonary arterial pressure in normal condition?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The reference mean pulmonary arterial pressure is about 15 mmHg.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of decreased alveolar oxygen on local alveolar blood flow?
options: By increasing vascular resistance, blood flow decreases
By decreasing vascular resistance, blood flow increases
By increasing vascular resistance, blood flow increases
By decreasing vascular resistance, blood flow decreases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Alveolar hypoxia constricts local pulmonary arterioles, increasing resistance and diverting blood away.

questions.prompt: What happens to the rate of oxygen diffusion with a doubling of the thickness of the respiratory membrane?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Fick diffusion is inversely proportional to membrane thickness with other factors fixed.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following centers controls normal and quite inspiration and respiratory rhythm?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: DRG is the traditional exam answer for quiet inspiratory drive. Modern rhythm generation also involves ventral pre-Botzinger networks; the pneumotaxic center primarily limits inspiration.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is likely the primary stimulus of the neurons in chemosensitive area?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: H+ in brain extracellular fluid is the direct central chemosensitive stimulus; CO2 acts largely through its production.

questions.prompt: What is the chloride shift in RBC of venous blood?
options: HCO3- goes into the cell and chloride ion goes out of the cell
Chloride ion goes out of the cell and H+ goes into the cell
H+ goes into the cell and chloride ion goes out of the cell
Chloride ion goes into the cell and HCO3- goes out of the cell
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At systemic tissues, bicarbonate leaves RBCs in exchange for chloride entry. Options B and C repeat the same incorrect direction.

questions.prompt: What is the cause of "physiological shunt" occurrence?
options: A decrease in ventilation/perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to zero
Mixture of pulmonary vein blood with bronchial vein blood
An increase in VA/Q ratio more than normal amount
A decrease in the cardiac output to half
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Both A (perfused unventilated units) and B (anatomical venous admixture) contribute to physiological shunt. No unique single answer; the source marks A.

questions.prompt: The maximum amount of CO2 is carried by the blood in the form of .....
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Bicarbonate is the dominant CO2 transport form. Carboxyhemoglobin is CO bound to hemoglobin, not the principal CO2 carrier.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a major function of the Upper Track?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Upper conducting airways condition air; significant respiratory gas exchange occurs distally.

questions.prompt: Which one the following causes a shift to the right in the O2 dissociation curve?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased CO2 shifts the oxygen dissociation curve right. The source star selects increased pH (B), which shifts it left; audited answer is C.

questions.prompt: In the lungs, which one of the following is NOT a barrier to gas exchange between capillary and the alveolar space?
options: A fluid layer of water and surfactants covering the luminal surface of alveolar cells
Basement membranes of endothelial and alveolar cells
Smooth muscle cells surrounding the endothelial cells
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The thin blood-air barrier has epithelial, basement-membrane and endothelial components; a smooth-muscle layer is absent.

questions.prompt: What is "the maximum amount of air that can be expired after a maximum inspiration"?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Vital capacity is the exhalable volume between maximal inspiration and maximal expiration.

questions.prompt: Which of the following occur during normal inspiration?
options: Diaphragm contracts, pleural pressure increases, alveolar pressure decreases
Diaphragm relaxes, external intercostals contract, pleural pressure increases
External and internal intercostals contract, pleural and alveolar pressure increase
Diaphragm contracts, pleural and alveolar pressures decrease
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diaphragm contraction lowers pleural pressure and transiently lowers alveolar pressure below atmospheric pressure during airflow.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is CORRECT about pulmonary surfactant?
options: Leads to a decreases in respiratory work
Is produced in type I alveolar cells
Most of its composition is related to proteins
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant lowers surface tension and inflation work; it is secreted by type II cells and is lipid-rich.

questions.prompt: Which one the following factor has no effect on distribution of pulmonary blood flow in different zones of the lung?
options: Change position from standing to lie down
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: C is the intended classical West-zone comparison: gravity, exercise and posture directly change vascular pressure relationships. The wording is simplified; surface tension can have indirect mechanical effects.

questions.prompt: Which part of the lung is zone 3 blood flow during lie down position?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The course's simplified supine model describes continuous zone-3 flow throughout the lung. Real regional conditions depend on vertical position and pressures.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be seen in the medial wall of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The maxillary nasal crest supports the septum; the other structures are lateral-wall landmarks.

questions.prompt: All of the following bones are involved in the formation of the posterior nostril (choanae) except?...
options: the medial plate of the pterygoid
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Choanal boundaries include vomer, palatine and sphenoid (medial pterygoid plate), not maxilla.

questions.prompt: Which of the following nerve is seen in incisive chanal?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The nasopalatine nerve traverses the incisive canal.

questions.prompt: Vomer articulates with all the following bones except?...
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vomer articulates with ethmoid, sphenoid, paired maxillae and palatines; not frontal bone.

questions.prompt: All of the following are correct about Trachea except?...
options: Ring-shaped cartilage is involved in its structure
The place where it bifurcates is around the sternal angle.
It is approximately 10 to 12 cm long.
The last cartilage is called carina trachea.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: A is the intended answer if ring-shaped means complete rings, because tracheal rings are C-shaped and posteriorly incomplete. D is also anatomically imprecise: the carina is the internal ridge at bifurcation, not simply the last cartilage. With these two questionable statements, no unique audited key is assigned.

questions.prompt: About the larynx, all the following options are correct except?...
options: Cuneiform cartilages are located in the thickness of the aryepiglottic folds.
The saccule opens to the ventricle in the middle chamber.
The inlet of the larynx is completely cartilaginous.
In deep breathing, the inlet of the larynx is completely open.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The laryngeal inlet includes soft aryepiglottic folds and is not wholly cartilaginous.

questions.prompt: All of the following options are correct except.....?
options: Arytenoid cartilages go to abduction position during breathing.
Arytenoid cartilages go to adduction position at the time of speaking.
Vocal cartilages are near the midline at the time of swallowing.
Arytenoid cartilages go to adduction position in deep breathing.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Deep inspiration requires abduction rather than adduction. The source term vocal cartilages is retained although vocal folds is the usual term.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is connected to thyroid cartilage?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Vocalis is part of thyroarytenoid and attaches anteriorly to thyroid cartilage.

questions.prompt: All of the following are true about the left lung except?...
options: The esophagus is adjacent to it.
Two deep fissure can be seen in it.
The most anterior element in the umbilicus of the lung is the pulmonary vein.
The lowest element in the umbilicus of the lung is the pulmonary vein.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The usual left lung has one oblique fissure; two fissures characterize the usual right lung. Umbilicus is source wording for hilum.

questions.prompt: Middle conchae is seen in which of the following bones?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The middle concha is part of ethmoid.

questions.prompt: All the following options are correct except?...
options: The lymph of the anterior areas of the nasal cavity is drained to the submandibular lymph nodes
Secretomotor innervation to the glands of the nasal cavities is in charge of parasympathetic.
The anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries are separated from the ophthalmic artery in the orbit
The great palatine artery passes through the sphenopalatine foramen and enters the nasal cavity
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The sphenopalatine artery passes through the sphenopalatine foramen; greater palatine reaches the anterior septum via the incisive canal.

questions.prompt: All of the following options are correct except?
options: The ethmoidal bulla is located in the middle meatus.
The crista galli is located in the upper meatus.
The ethmoid cribriform plate separates the nasal cavity from the cranial cavity.
The ethmoidal infundibulum extends forward and upward below the bulla.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Crista galli projects intracranially from ethmoid; it is not a superior-meatus structure.

questions.prompt: Where is the Olfactory cell located?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Olfactory receptor neurons occur in specialized nasal olfactory mucosa.

questions.prompt: What is the name Macrophage In Alveolar Of Lung Tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The source selects Pneumocyte III, an unsupported/nonstandard label for an alveolar macrophage. The review distinguishes macrophages (dust cells) from epithelial pneumocytes; no standard correct option is supplied.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is observed true vocal cord?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: True vocal folds are laryngeal structures.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is observed simple squamous epithelial tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Alveolar ducts are bounded predominantly by alveolar openings with type I squamous lining. Respiratory Duct is not a standard distinct airway label; retained verbatim.

questions.prompt: Which of the following these observed Hyaline Cartilage Tissue
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The larynx clearly includes hyaline cartilages, but vestibular nasal support also includes hyaline cartilage. Without specifying mucosa versus supporting wall, the marked A and option C cannot be separated reliably.

questions.prompt: Terminal bronchiole appears in which stage of lung maturity?
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: The conducting tree through terminal bronchioles develops during the pseudoglandular period; respiratory bronchioles develop in the canalicular period.

questions.prompt: All the following options are correct except...?
options: Breathing movements of the lung in fetus appear before birth.
Alveolar epithelial cells type 2 secrete surfactant.
Laryngeal cartilages originate from the mesenchyme of the third pharyngeal arch.
The inner lining of the larynx is endodermal.
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Laryngeal cartilages derive from fourth/sixth arch mesenchyme, not third arch; epithelium is endodermal.

questions.prompt: All the following options are correct except...?
options: Cartilaginous parts of trachea and lung are from visceral mesoderm.
Respiratory diverticulum appears in the fetus in the fourth week of pregnancy.
The lung bud is a protrusion on the dorsal surface of the forgut.
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: The lung bud projects from ventral foregut. Polyhydramnios is particularly associated with esophageal atresia accompanying TEF; the source's generalization is imprecise.

audit.notes: All preferred source images visually reviewed; OCR used only as a drafting aid. All supplied complete items retained. Source annotations are unofficial, preserved separately from the audited answer. Null audited keys deliberately quarantine ambiguous or defective questions. Numbered options 1-4 and Persian letters are normalized to A-D in displayed order.
